answer: [REDACTED] is a single mediating [REDACTED]: INDEX.json lists every installed capability as a compact record (id, kind, selector_tags, summary, body_rel, activation_cost_processes, deactivate_method). [REDACTED].select scores tag overlap against the index and does not load bodies. [REDACTED].activate materializes the body and, for mcp_mount, spawns a stdio child; [REDACTED].deactivate runs the kind-specific path (unload-context / unregister-dispatcher / unload-rule-table / drop-compiled-stages / drop-overlay / reap-stdio-child) and returns the session to the measured floor. When nothing is selected the resident set is 1 process and 5596 bytes (INDEX.json + [REDACTED].json + index.schema.json). The always-on baseline of the same inventory, measured with the same resident() function, is 3 processes and 10109 bytes. Per-session budget max_activated_processes=1 max_activated_bytes=20000 on_exhaustion=REFUSE: the second MCP mount is refused and not spawned. NOT_INSTALLED (absent from index) is distinct from not_selected (in index, below threshold). The FIRST construct that is not expressible as an index record without activation is a capability whose match criterion is only a runtime side-effect of executing its body (no static selector_tags).

precedence.budget_vs_selection: A selected id may still be REFUSED at activate() when the session budget is exhausted. Refusal is not a select miss.
precedence.duplicate_in_one_file: FAIL-CLOSED: the index is invalid and the [REDACTED] refuses to start.
precedence.loader: JSON Schema validate + id uniqueness + body existence check. No evaluator.
precedence.merge: No field-level merge of index records. Replacement is whole-record on a future overlay; this prototype has a single INDEX.json.
precedence.not_installed: An id absent from the index is NOT_INSTALLED. Select never invents ids.
precedence.rule: INDEX.json is the discovery SSOT. A body file is materialized only after activate(id) for an installed record. Generated or hand-copied bodies do not become discoverable until indexed.
precedence.tie_break: Duplicate ids in INDEX.json FAIL-CLOSED (load aborts). No timestamp, mtime, or runtime coin-flip.
